standfirst: A demon loses his powers, a cynical heiress becomes the battery he needs, and they sign a marriage contract. The first four hours are a genuinely fun supernatural romcom and the next twelve are an inheritance war nobody asked for. These six do the same premise with more discipline.

picks.why: A demon in a Seoul institution, learning humans by force. Closest match in the catalog: same fish-out-of-hell comedy, same slow discovery that the assignment matters. Difference: it has a case-of-the-week engine, so it never has to invent filler the way My Demon does from episode nine.

The immortal and the girl whose existence is the loophole. My Demon is built on the Goblin shape: a being who cannot die, a contract written in fate, and a rule that makes love lethal. Difference: Goblin actually pays its mythology off, and its ending asks something real of both leads.

Supernatural boyfriend, mortal woman, ancient debt. Same balance of urban fantasy and comedy, with action scenes the budget can support. Difference: the sibling rivalry gives the back half a villain with a motive, which is precisely what My Demon lacks.

A bound magical being and the human holding the contract. The wish mechanics do the work the demon powers do here, and the comedy comes from the same power imbalance. Difference: it goes somewhere sad, and it means it.

Contract relationship played for pure comedy. If the marriage-of-convenience beats were your reason for staying, this is the cleanest version of them. Difference: no fantasy layer at all, so nothing has to obey magic rules that keep changing.

Interspecies romance with a countdown attached. Same setup of a non-human learning to want a specific person, same glossy production. Difference: the mythology is tighter and the ending will split the room.

against.title: Hotel del Luna
against.why: The reflex pick for supernatural romance. It is a grief drama with a thousand-year backstory and a firm moral position on death. My Demon is a romcom that treats hell as a HR department.

against.title: Doom at Your Service
against.why: Paired because it is also a fantasy contract with a deadline. That show is about dying, honestly and slowly. Bringing that expectation here is a mismatch.

against.title: Alchemy of Souls
against.why: Named as the other big fantasy romance of the era. The magic system there is load-bearing and the world has rules; My Demon rewrites its own whenever the couple needs a scene.
